knowledge:
- key_parameters: ribosomal=logical indicating whether to calculate CU bias/expressivity with respect to ribosomal genes ;; filtering=character ('hard' or 'soft') to handle sequences shorter than a threshold ;; len.threshold=numeric threshold in codons for filtering short sequences (default 80) ;; subsets=named list of annotations, logical vectors, or codon count tables for custom reference sets ;; target=character ('pathway', 'module', or 'cog') for mapping KO categories to broader ontologies in reduceCrossTab() ;; threshold=numeric value to define highly expressed genes in crossTab() ;; percentiles=numeric value to define highly expressed genes as a top percentage in crossTab()
- alternatives: MILC() can be substituted with other CU statistics like B(), MCB(), ENCprime(), ENC(), or SCUO() ;; MELP() can be substituted with other expressivity measures like E(), CAI(), GCB(), or Fop()
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing codon usage bias in prokaryotic genomes or metagenomes, predicting relative gene expression levels based on translational optimization, and identifying enriched functional categories among highly expressed genes.
- pitfalls: CU statistics are highly dependent on sequence length, so filtering out sequences shorter than 80 codons (using filtering='hard') is strongly recommended ;; If sequences are filtered during CU calculation, annotations must be filtered by the same length threshold before plotting or downstream analysis to maintain alignment ;; ENC() and SCUO() do not accept reference subsets because they measure distance to uniform codon usage.

workflows.name: codon_usage_and_enrichment_analysis
workflows.intent: Analyze codon usage bias, predict gene expressivity, and perform functional enrichment analysis on highly expressed genes from DNA sequences.
input: sequences.fasta (FASTA file containing DNA sequences of open reading frames)
workflows.stages: 1. Load DNA sequences and convert to a codonTable object ;; 2. Calculate codon usage bias with optional filtering ;; 3. Visualize codon usage bias ;; 4. Predict gene expressivity ;; 5. Create a contingency table of annotations and expressivity values ;; 6. Reduce the contingency table to broader ontologies ;; 7. Perform functional enrichment analysis ;; 8. Visualize enrichment results ;; 9. Integrate multiple samples into a single matrix
workflows.code:
dnaLD94 <- readSet(
  file="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BioinfoHR/coRdon-examples/master/LD94.fasta"
)
LD94 <- codonTable(dnaLD94)
dnaHD59 <- readSet(
  file="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BioinfoHR/coRdon-examples/master/HD59.fasta"
)
HD59 <- codonTable(dnaHD59)
cc <- codonCounts(HD59)
l <- getlen(HD59)
length(HD59)
ko <- getKO(HD59)
milc <- MILC(HD59, ribosomal = TRUE, filtering = "hard")
Bplot(x = "ribosomal", y = "self", data = milc_HD59)
genes <- getKO(HD59)[getlen(HD59) > 80]
Bplot(x = "ribosomal", y = "self", data = milc,
        annotations = genes, ribosomal = TRUE)
intraBplot(HD59, LD94, names = c("HD59", "LD94"), 
            variable = "MILC", 
            ribosomal = TRUE)
melp <- MELP(HD59, ribosomal = TRUE, filtering = "hard")
ct <- crossTab(genes, as.numeric(melp), threshold = 1L)
contable(ct)
ann <- getSeqAnnot(ct)
var <- getVariable(ct)
enr <- enrichment(ct)
enr_data <- pData(enr)
enrichMAplot(enr, pvalue = "pvals", siglev = 0.05)
ctpath <- reduceCrossTab(ct, target = "pathway")
enrpath <- enrichment(ctpath)
enrpath_data <- pData(enrpath)
enrichBarplot(enrpath, variable = "enrich", 
                pvalue = "padj", siglev = 0.05)
mat <- enrichMatrix(list(HD59 = enrHD59, LD94 = enrLD94), 
                    variable = "enrich")
